fields.Q1:
WHAT IS STANDING AROUND THIS ROOM MADE OF?**
Coursed stone blocks — dry, dressed, sandy-grey, laid in horizontal courses about 30px (15 native px) tall. But that's only true of the wall running east-west at y≈390–425. The two walls flanking the north corridor (x≈315–373 and x≈441–499) I cannot name as a material. They are horizontal bands of soft mottled tan. Nothing on them says stone, or brick, or anything else. I'd be guessing.
fields.Q1_WHY: The east-west course at y 390–425 has readable block divisions — I found dark 2px separators at x = 80, 284, 318, 509, 565, 603, 637, spacings 34–71px, irregular enough not to look stamped. That reads as masonry. The corridor walls have horizontal lines at y ≈ 140, 183, 217, 246, 281, 311, 344, 374 (left) and **not one vertical joint anywhere**. I scanned rows at y=240, 300, 340, 380, 410 across the full 57px width of each band, normalised for the light falloff: the deepest dip is 0.91 of local mean. There is no dark line. That is 325 pixels of wall — thirteen courses — with nothing crossing them. Coursed stone that never breaks a course isn't stone. It's stripes.
fields.Q2:
SOLID MASS, OR A FLAT PATTERN AROUND THE EDGE?**
**Flat pattern.** The wall has no thickness anywhere in this image. At x=300, scanning down through the south wall: y=388 is void (17,12,8), y=390 jumps to (127,91,59), y=394 reaches (164,118,75), holds ~160 for 26px, then a 2px seam at y=422, then floor. No cap, no lip, no top face distinct from a side face, no highlight on the near edge. The wall is one flat band butted against one flat void. Same at the corridor: x=374 is (140,100,64), x=375 is (42,31,20) — one step, and the dark seam that follows is the identical 2px separator used between every block in the frame, not a shadow.
fields.Q3:
WHERE EXACTLY DOES THE GROUND STOP?**
It doesn't stop at a wall — it stops at a stencil. The boundary at x=310, y=160–380: x=310 reads (1,1,2), x=311 reads 11–77 depending on height. **One pixel.** Zero transition. Nothing gets darker, nothing occludes, no contact shading. Same on the horizontal at y=133 (col x=100: 12,12,12,12 then 1,1,1,1). The edge is a perfectly axis-aligned rectangle cut, and it runs mid-block through whatever it crosses.
fields.Q4:
WHAT IS HOLDING THIS PLACE TOGETHER?**
**NOTHING.** There is not one fastener, tie, brace, pin, prop, rope, strap, wedge, timber, or patch anywhere in the frame. Given a four-hundred-year garrison that repairs endlessly with rope, driven pins, hide and salvaged timber, that is the loudest thing in the picture. I looked at every lit surface. The only two non-wall objects are both pure black silhouettes: a stemmed, four-barred shape at x≈133–142, y≈388–418, and a plain vertical bar at x≈566–570, y≈378–400. Both are filled at the same value as the void, with zero interior detail, so they read as holes in the wall rather than things fixed to it.
fields.Q5:
BUILT, OR AN IMAGE THAT WAS REPEATED?**
**Repeated.** I de-vignetted the left corridor wall and compared its courses to each other. Courses at y 183–217 vs 250–283 differ by 0.020; y 250–283 vs 313–348 by 0.014; y 220–250 vs 348–377 by 0.017. Unrelated pairs sit at 0.049–0.080. The wall is two stripe motifs alternating, tiled downward — course N and course N+2 are the same image. Nothing on it was placed.
fields.Q6:
WOULD YOU BELIEVE THIS SHIPPED IN A COMMERCIAL GAME?**
**YES.** Plenty of mobile roguelikes ship walls no better than this.

Merely competent. Not good. The south course is competent. The corridor walls are a gradient with lines on it, and the boundary treatment is a stencil cut with no craft in it at all.
fields.Q7:
AT THE SIZE SHOWN, WHAT CAN YOU ACTUALLY SEE ON THE STANDING SURFACES?**
At 1:1, on the brightest wall in the frame — the east-west course at y 390–425, x 250–560 — I can see it is divided into blocks, and I can see the blocks are soft-shaded rather than flat. That is all. On the corridor walls I can see horizontal banding on the left one (x 315–373, y 240–400) and, honestly, almost nothing on the right one. No joint, no chisel mark, no chip, no stain, no patch, no seam between courses that I'd call detail. The faces are blank.

Magnifying adds: the 2px separators, the soft blob mottling inside each block, and the absence of vertical joints. None of that is new information — it's the confirmation that there was nothing to see.

It falls apart with distance fast. At y=240 the corridor walls sit at 24–33; at y=160 they are 10–13, identical to the general dark field, and the corridor floor between them is 6–9. Above roughly y=200 you cannot tell wall from corridor from empty screen.
fields.Q7_WHY: Checked at 1:1 — (250,390)-(560,425) south course; (315,240)-(373,400) left corridor wall; (441,240)-(499,400) right corridor wall; (60,390)-(250,425) west end of the south course. Magnified — (368,330)-(392,350) at the wall/floor seam; (280,120)-(420,300) at the void corner; (100,370)-(320,440) for the black object; (295,60)-(520,450) at 3x for the whole corridor.
fields.Q8:
IS THERE ANYTHING YOUR EYE KEEPS RETURNING TO?**
Yes, three things.

The horizontal banding on the left corridor wall — because it is the only rhythm on screen and it never varies. Once you see the ~30px pitch you cannot stop counting it down from y=140 to y=393.

The two black silhouettes at (137, 400) and (568, 390). They are the same value as the void rectangles, so every time the eye passes them it re-reads them as gaps in the wall and has to correct.

The right corridor wall, x 441–499 — I keep going back because there is nothing there. I detected three course lines over 260px against eight on the left wall at the same distance from the light. The two walls of one corridor are not built to the same standard.
fields.Q9:
WHAT IS BEYOND THE WALLS?**
Flat fill. Not another room, not darkness, not more stone — a single colour. I sampled the left rectangle (10,140)–(305,390): 78% of pixels are exactly (1,1,2), and the rest are the torchlight gradient. Down the column x=150 it is (1,1,2) unbroken from y=140 to y=320. Across y=370 it climbs 1 → 2 → 3 → 5 → 7 → 10 → 12 → 15 as you approach the corridor, warm-tinted.

That last part is the problem. **The torchlight is being drawn onto the void.** The wall does not block the light — the lighting pass paints straight through it onto the flat fill behind. Under a gamma lift the light circle's arc is plainly visible crossing both rectangles from x≈100 to x≈700. So beyond the wall is not space and not solid; it is a hole in the artwork that the renderer lights as if it were floor.
fields.Q10:
COULD YOU TELL A WAY THROUGH FROM A DEAD END WITHOUT WALKING INTO IT?**
Found it: the gap at x 375–437 in the east-west course, directly north of the figure at (405,485).

**I read it as a passage.** Two things did it. The crisp mortar-joint floor texture runs continuously through the gap and up the corridor — same grid, same cracks, an unbroken diagonal crack crossing y≈500 to y≈300. And the flanking material changes character at the gap edge: floor grid on the inside, unjointed bands on the outside. That contrast is the whole read.

It only works close in. By y≈200 the corridor floor is at 6–9 and the walls are at 10–13, and the distinction is gone. The passage is legible for about 200 pixels and then stops being legible — not because it gets dark, but because the two materials converge to the same value.
fields.Q11:
HAS ANYTHING HAPPENED TO THIS STRUCTURE?**
Nothing has happened to it. It is unweathered, unbroken, unmended, and unused. Every course line is straight, every block edge is square, no stone is displaced, chipped, spalled, soot-stained, or replaced. I read that from the course lines at y 140/183/217/246/281/311/344/374 running perfectly horizontal and unbroken across the full 57px band, and from the block separators in the south course all being the same clean 2px width at the same value.

The brief says continuous heavy use since before records begin, never cared for, and a garrison that has been patching it for four centuries. The standing structure shows evidence of none of that. It looks like it was laid last week and nobody has walked past it since.
fields.CULL: Walls are unjointed repeating stripes; void is flat fill the torchlight shines straight through.
fields.FLIP LIST:
- Break every course on the corridor walls (x 315–373, x 441–499) with vertical joints on an irregular pitch — no course may run more than ~60px unbroken.
- Give the wall a top edge: a 2–4px lighter cap along y=389 and along x=310/505, so the mass reads as having thickness rather than as a stencil cut.
- Stop the torchlight at the wall. The void rectangles must not receive the light gradient — the ramp from (1,1,2) to (15,11,7) across x 110→285 at y=370 is the wall failing to occlude.
- Kill the 2-course repeat on the left wall (y 183–217 ≡ 250–283 ≡ 313–348) and bring the right wall up to the left wall's detail density — it currently carries 3 course lines to the left's 8.
- Put the garrison's repairs on the walls where the light reaches: driven pins, lashed rope, hide, salvaged timber across the south course at y 390–425, x 250–560. Right now nothing in the frame has ever been touched.

---

Worth flagging for whatever comes next: the void-lighting bug and the stencil edge are one problem, not two — both say the wall isn't an object in the renderer, it's a hole in a floor bitmap. Fixing the cap and the joints will make the corridor read, but until the wall occludes light it will keep feeling like a picture of a room rather than a room.

*Model: Claude Opus 5 (1M context)*
